claims.text: The identity of X (Si, Mn, or Al) governs whether a stable, coherent protective oxide forms and persists on CrFeCoNiX alloys above 900 °C.
Si-containing CrFeCoNiX forms a SiO2-rich protective surface layer.
Al-containing CrFeCoNiX forms an Al2O3-rich protective surface layer.
Cr2O3 may support the SiO2- or Al2O3-rich protective layer.
The SiO2- or Al2O3-rich scales are slow-growing and adherent.
The proposed SiO2- or Al2O3-rich scales minimize oxygen and cation diffusion.
The proposed SiO2- or Al2O3-rich scales reduce thermal-mismatch stresses.
Mn-containing CrFeCoNi forms a mixed oxide scale that is more prone to cracking and spallation than the scales on Si- or Al-containing variants.
The composition, thickness, and coherence of the oxide scale mediate its protective behavior.
Si and Al favor protective low-growth-rate oxides because those oxides have high thermodynamic stability and low diffusivity.
Low oxide growth rate leads to a well-adhered and coherent scale.
Mn-bearing oxides have higher diffusivity than the proposed Si- or Al-bearing protective oxides.
Mn-bearing oxides have greater thermal-expansion mismatch, causing stress accumulation and eventual cracking or spallation.
Under identical high-temperature oxidative conditions, the Si- and Al-containing alloys will have lower spallation and less surface degradation than CrFeCoNiMn.
The proposed mechanism applies to single- or multiphase metallic solid solutions above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres.
Known effects in other alloy systems support the general trend that Si and Al promote protective oxides.
